title: Cahokia: achievement, evidence and limits
instructions: Read the original practice passage and answer all questions. This is a shorter practice set, not a full IELTS Reading section.

stimulus.text:
A. The following adapted reading presents the course text’s account of Cahokia, not a new archaeological assessment. A community beside the Mississippi developed from a village into a major urban centre. The text places it within the society of the Mississippians and compares its scale in the eleventh century with London’s. It presents the settlement as sophisticated and outward-looking rather than as an isolated collection of dwellings. The comparison is intended to establish its urban significance. It is not a claim that its buildings or institutions were identical to those of a European city.

B. Archaeological work in the account suggests that roughly thirty-five percent of the population came from elsewhere. The text connects this unusual movement of people with a possible explanation: planners redesigned the village and made it attractive to surrounding communities. The explanation is presented as a theory rather than direct knowledge of every migrant’s motives. Few comparable examples of tribal relocation had been found by the researchers described. The evidence concerns population movement; the proposed attraction remains an interpretation of that evidence.

C. Carrying out the plans involved substantial labour. The inhabitants moved soil in baskets and by hand rather than with machinery, creating 120 mounds. The largest reached a height of about 100 feet. Buildings and a large plaza formed part of the new urban environment. The passage then describes cooperation in construction, hunting, fishing, cultivation and household work. Together these details show a community implementing ambitious plans through coordinated effort. The scale of the result is contrasted with the available means, not used to imply that mechanical equipment must have been present.

D. Despite its activity and growth, Cahokia was largely abandoned by 1350 after becoming a major population centre around 1050. The course account emphasises that its decline remains unexplained. Weapons found at other sites were absent here, and the text does not consider familiar explanations such as European invasion sufficient in this case. That absence does not reveal a replacement cause. It limits what can confidently be concluded.

E. Archaeological discoveries also give a mixed picture of life. Jewellery, cooking pots and a small workshop reveal everyday activities and skilled work. The account then turns to much darker findings: mass burials and evidence interpreted as frequent human sacrifice, especially involving young women. It does not claim to know with certainty whether the motive was religious or something else. Admiration for the city’s achievements consequently coexists with disturbing evidence about its practices.

options.text: The objects give evidence of everyday activities.
The account establishes religious motives for all the sacrifices.
The discoveries include disturbing findings.

options.text: The explanation is repeated.
The explanation comes later than another.
A satisfactory explanation is not supplied.

criteria.label: Textual evidence
criteria.description: Select or supply the answer warranted by this passage, observing the response limit and distinction between contradiction and absence.

answerKey.rationale: A establishes urban significance through a comparison without asserting identity.
B distinguishes population movement from a theory of its cause.
C connects manual methods, scale and cooperation.
D emphasises unexplained abandonment and limits of familiar explanations.
E balances everyday artefacts with sacrifice evidence while retaining motive uncertainty.
D has just contrasted weapons at other sites with their absence at Cahokia; the following sentence limits inference from it.
E explicitly leaves religious versus other motives uncertain.
Un- negates explained, fitting D’s stated uncertainty.

assessment.feedbackGuidance: After submission compare a selected heading with the whole paragraph: state its central message and the modifier that made the strongest rival wrong. Do not accept matching nouns as sufficient. For reference and prefix items, explain both the antecedent or affix and the surrounding context. Ask for a revised one-sentence paragraph summary; use a new context next. Raw accuracy is not a band.
